title: Sufficient aid divided into efficacious and inefficacious by its outcome
source_text: LXXIX. Inde est quod auxilium sufficiens dividit in auxilium efficax, & auxilium inefficax. Auxilium efficax est quod sequitur effectus, id est, bonum opus ad quod hominem movet. Inefficax vero quod caret effectu, & per quod homo actu non convertitur, nec bene operatur.
pass_a_gloss: LXXIX. Thence it is that he divides sufficient help into efficacious help, and inefficacious help. Efficacious help is that which the effect follows, that is, the good work to which it moves the man. But inefficacious that which lacks effect, and through which the man is not actually converted, nor works well.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXXIX. Hence he divides sufficient aid into efficacious and inefficacious aid. Efficacious aid is the aid that its effect follows, that is, the good work to which it moves a person. Inefficacious aid lacks its effect: through it a person is not actually converted and does not act well.

lemmas.gloss: he divides sufficient help into efficacious help, and inefficacious help

choices.why: Molina's division of sufficient aid by its outcome; terms kept as in the locus.

bible_refs: Luis de Molina SJ, Concordia liberi arbitrii cum gratiae donis (Lisbon, 1588), question 14, article 13.
